run.question:
Alertmanager alert PendingPodsDetected (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/otel-demo since 2026-11-15T10:44:59Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The PendingPodsDetected alert for namespace otel-demo is explained by a configuration change in two Deployments, ad and cart: their pod templates now carry nodeSelector {kubernetes.io/hostname: invalid-node}. No node in the cluster has that hostname label, so the ReplicaSets created at 2026-11-15T10:44:02Z (ad-dd7f45975) and 2026-11-15T10:44:10Z (cart-5b597c6db5) each created one pod that the scheduler reports as Unschedulable (PodScheduled=False), which matches the 2 pending pods the alert annotations report. The pods are Pending only because they were never scheduled, not because of resource pressure, eviction, OOM kills, image pulls or application crashes. The previous ReplicaSets of both Deployments (ad-554b849958, cart-755465879b) still hold their 1 available/ready replica and are the sole ready endpoints behind the ad and cart Services, so traffic continues to be served. Ownership chain deployment -> replica set -> pod verified for both workloads; the container image is unchanged (ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and :2.1.3-cart), consistent with a config-only rollout. No other pod in the cluster is Pending, and all other pods in otel-demo are Running and Ready with zero restarts.

claims.text: Exactly two pods in otel-demo are Pending: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p (created 2026-11-15T10:44:02Z) and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh (created 2026-11-15T10:44:10Z); both have no assigned node (.spec.nodeName empty). A cluster-wide pod query returned no Pending pod outside otel-demo (1 of 67 objects matched).

Both pending pods have status condition PodScheduled=False with reason Unschedulable and message "0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/5 nodes are available: 5 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling." Their containerStatuses lists are empty, i.e. no container was ever started.

Scheduler Warning events with reason FailedScheduling are recorded on ad-dd7f45975-mw86p (count 3, first 2026-11-15T10:44:02Z, last 2026-11-15T10:54:25Z) and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh (count 3, first 2026-11-15T10:44:10Z, last 2026-11-15T10:54:25Z), source default-scheduler, with the node affinity/selector message.

Both pending pods specify spec.nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"} with no affinity, and the pod templates of Deployments ad and cart both specify the same nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"}.

The cluster has 5 nodes whose kubernetes.io/hostname labels are i-01a47734339426210, i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15 and i-097278082719f10ba; none is named "invalid-node". Only i-01a47734339426210 carries the node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane NoSchedule taint; the other four are Ready without taints.

Ownership chain confirmed: pod ad-dd7f45975-mw86p is owned by ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 (created 2026-11-15T10:44:02Z), which is owned by Deployment ad; pod cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh is owned by ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5 (created 2026-11-15T10:44:10Z), owned by Deployment cart. Both new ReplicaSets have 1 desired replica, no readyReplicas and the invalid-node nodeSelector in their template, while the older ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 (created 10:06:37Z) and cart-755465879b (created 10:06:36Z) each have 1 available replica and no nodeSelector.

The two new ReplicaSets were populated by their own controller: Normal events SuccessfulCreate "Created pod: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p" at 10:44:02Z on ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 and "Created pod: cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh" at 10:44:10Z on ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5, source replicaset-controller.

Deployment ad reports generation 2, annotation deployment.kubernetes.io/revision "2", helm release name otel-demo, spec.replicas 1, status replicas 2, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1, unavailableReplicas 1; Deployment cart reports the same generation 2, revision 2, helm release otel-demo and 1 unavailable replica. Both keep unchanged images ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart. All other 19 deployments in otel-demo are generation 1 with nodeSelector null, ready 1 and available 1.

Endpoints for Service ad contain only ad-554b849958-42mdm (100.96.3.180) and Endpoints for Service cart contain only cart-755465879b-bgb2p (100.96.3.205), with empty notReadyAddresses; the two Pending pods are not endpoints of either Service.

All other 21 pods in otel-demo are phase Running with Ready condition True and zero restarts, with no container in waiting state and no lastState.terminated entry (no CrashLoopBackOff, OOMKilled or Evicted evidence in the namespace).

Span counts from the surviving replicas continue through window end: service ad shows roughly 1198-1296 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans per 10m and service cart roughly 10851-11507 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans per 10m at every 5-minute step from 10:24:59Z to 10:59:59Z. Service ad additionally reports about 1.05 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans per 10m from the 10:34:59Z step onward, while cart has no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series in this query.

The trigger was a config-only rollout: Deployments ad and cart (both Helm-managed, meta.helm.sh/release-name=otel-demo) moved from generation 1 to generation 2 with the same image but a pod-template nodeSelector of kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node, producing the new unschedulable ReplicaSets at 10:44:02Z and 10:44:10Z, about 45 seconds before the alert start at 10:44:59Z. Who or what applied the change, and its exact source, cannot be verified because change history is not an available integration in this Run.

Node resource pressure or insufficient CPU/memory is not the cause: the scheduler message attributes 0/5 nodes to the control-plane taint and to pod node affinity/selector mismatch rather than to insufficient resources, and no pod in otel-demo shows Evicted events, OOMKilled terminations or any restarts.

The control-plane taint is not the cause: only 1 of the 5 nodes carries node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane, and the scheduler reports the other 4 nodes as failing on pod node affinity/selector, so the taint alone does not explain why these two pods are unschedulable.

Container-level failure such as image pull error, container crash or probe failure is not the cause for either pending pod: neither pod has any containerStatuses entry because no container was started, and the same images 2.1.3-ad and 2.1.3-cart are referenced by the older ReplicaSets whose pods are Running and Ready.

Remove the nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname: invalid-node from the ad and cart Deployment pod templates, or point it at an existing node hostname such as i-037e40963128cbd9f, then let the new ReplicaSets recreate their pods so the two Pending pods can be scheduled.

gaps: change_history is not an available integration in this Run, so who or what applied the nodeSelector change to Deployments ad and cart, and the exact change timestamp, could not be verified.

The metric query kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="otel-demo",phase="Pending"} == 1 returned no data (status no_data) for 09:44:59Z-11:00:00Z, so the pending count and its onset could not be corroborated from kube-state-metrics.

The rule lookup for PendingPodsDetected via list_prometheus_rules returned no data (status no_data), and a get_metric_names query for kube_pod_*/kube_deployment_* returned no data, so the exact alert expression and whether kube-state-metrics is scraped into this Prometheus could not be confirmed.

No comparable pre-change baseline exists for ad's STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans: the range query for STATUS_CODE_ERROR before 09:44:59Z (06:00:00Z-09:44:59Z) returned no data, and a Jaeger search for ad traces tagged error=true in 10:30:00Z-11:00:00Z returned no data, so whether roughly 1 error span per 10m is normal or related to this incident is unknown and no impact is claimed from it.

Deployment rolling-update strategy fields (maxSurge/maxUnavailable) were not read; that the old replicas were retained with unavailableReplicas 1 is read from status rather than from the strategy configuration.

Alertmanager-side state (silences, firing status, and the Prometheus instance that evaluated the rule) is not queryable here; only the alert labels and annotations supplied in the investigation context were used as leads.
next_steps: Review the otel-demo Helm values and release history for ad and cart to identify the edit that set nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node, since change history is not available in this environment.
After correcting the nodeSelector, confirm the new ReplicaSets reach readyReplicas 1, that ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh are gone, and that PendingPodsDetected resolves.

Locate the PendingPodsDetected rule definition in the alerting rule source and confirm whether kube-state-metrics should be scraped into this Prometheus so pending-pod state is observable as a metric.
